verdict.rationale: mParticle documents its own HTTP APIs (Events API with a downloadable OpenAPI spec, Warehouse Sync API, Platform Audiences API), so scripts can drive core functions without the UI. A per-batch development/production environment flag can separate test traffic, but it is not a sandbox. Nothing documents a CLI, CI integration, or headless runbooks, and some workflows such as connecting audience outputs are described as UI navigation. missing for 10: official CLI or CI tooling, documented CI/headless automation guides, OpenAPI specs beyond the Events API, an isolated sandbox/test tenant for CI runs, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Use the Open API (previously known as Swagger) specification or similar tools to generate helper SDKs (using Swagger Codegen or OpenAPI Generator) for the Events API
with a Warehouse Sync API, SQL reference, and data mapping
Every Events API batch carries an environment field, "production" or "development"
